Visually it's a pretty okay game, the hub looks like a cool castle-thing with loads of places to display some cool, presumably hidden artifacts.
There is no characters to interact with, no narrator, no voice whatsoever.
No quest, no helping anybody, no real threat.
I thought it would be a resource-gathering, exploratory game, but the resources you are after have zero rewarding factor to find. It's just random items with random value, and you sell everything for cash. Cash is what you farm for upgrading everything.
No "be on the look-out for purple crystals!" or "follow the climbing rope in hopes of finding better gear that helps you weather the cold!"
Nothing like that whatsoever, which unfortunately makes it feel very soul-less and slapped together with no love or care. The way the snow melts is also very gimmick-y, with chunks left floating in the air, no physics, no animation, just textures getting replaced rapidly while you hold left mouse button and wave the cursor around. There is no real perception of depth, either, sometimes making it difficult to judge if you're standing on a hill of snow or not, if you're too far away to melt the next chunk or not.
Unfortunately kind of reminiscent of one of those adds you get on your phone for a generic "game", that yes, technically has some kind of functional principle, but basically just feels like busywork.
Not even the achievements are thoughtful.
"Use your hook 30 times."
"Use your hook 50 times."

No "I hate snow! - Clear 99% of the snow from your first area", since you can technically get through every area by just melting a path through the middle of the wall of snow. It's not even dangerous to do that, because nothing will collapse - There's no physics with snow even floating in the air, remember?

The second area reminds me of a platformer level, jumping from one sheet of ice to the next. Only there is no need to do so, the "pit" you'd cross that way has stairs on both ends, and you have a grappling hook by the time you get to that part anyway, so you just end up jump-grappling to skip ahead. The sluggish-feeling controls make it near impossible to time jumps right anyway.

The upgrading system is generous, assuring quick progress, but have a seemingly random cost-jump.
Upgrades become more costly in steps, starting at $10, $30, $50, $75, reasonable steps until about $300, then suddenly there's a huge jump to $2100.

All-in-all, pretty heartless and monotonous.

What I liked: the intro was funny to me, the animations for upgrading the meltgun and the teslagun were really good, removing the snow felt pretty good, the two different kinds of snow was interesting as well, the grapple hook was fun to use, and collecting the ice cubes to melt helped with feeling goal oriented. I also liked the sudden shifts from snow cave to stone room. I liked the details in the main room with all the books, potions, and even swords behind doors. I adored the transition of the mammoth. how pristine it was and then when it was burned, it was all charred after the credits.

What I disliked: the autosave freezing the whole game, backpack capacity capping at 100. doesn't feel proportional to how much the guns get upgraded, I had to do too many run backs that felt completely tedious. nearly quit and refunded. there was no lore. I got zero information about what I was doing, why I was doing it until the very end. the repetitive items that dropped from the snow were boring, to say the least. I kept wondering how many people died in the snow from all the boots and goggles... didn't like the platforming sections, just a bit clunky and had to run jump each platform when they were close. needs more boost when jumping to feel a little smoother, I think. a reluctant thumbs up

review/final thoughts, with a slight spoiler, i guess

It's a fun overall idea for a game, it's like 'a game about digging hole' except expanded on and reversed in the order you get the tools.  

As it stands now i'm stuck and have no clue where to go to get the last 2 relics on the bottom floor, and last mastodon bone or whatever they're called.  I have all 3 tools and all upgrades.  I've backtracked over the whole map several times now, making sure to thoroughly explore all paths to make sure i didn't miss anything.  And i can't find a wall to bomb, or door, or spot with stuff to mine out anywhere.  The layout is so overly confusing for the sake of being confusing.

The shovel is entirely pointless and i'm quite baffled why it's even in here, especially as the last tool after you've been using a maxed out tesla vacuum for hours.  You don't even get an upgrade to make it work automatically, so instead you have to click each time.  Again, just a baffling design decision all around.

Technical issues are a plenty, tons of audio bugs, tons of texture issues with misaligned textures and areas were you can see behind or under or over textures, mechanical bugs where sometimes the 3 star frost would take damage away like it should, but then coming back through it wouldn't take any damage away, so that made no sense.  Collision issues where you would find an object/surface with collision detection but no visible textures, so you just start going up an invisible ramp and can't get to where you're trying to go without going around the invisible surface.

Again, it's a fun game and a neat idea, if not heavily borrowing from 'a game about digging a hole', but it's just full of bugs and technical issues and strange design decisions.

I have to say, anyone who enjoys this type of game will have a good time. It isn't particularly deep, but it offers a fresh take on the concept.

The basic premise—the core idea—remains the same, though instead of digging downwards through tunnels, you move horizontally.

The paths can be quite confusing—especially if you lack a good sense of direction (which was certainly the case for me! xd).

It was a bit frustrating for me at times, though that was really just a "me problem" during the early stages (xd).


If you like this genre, you'll enjoy yourself; if not... well, you know how it goes (xd).
I’ve encountered two bugs so far, but nothing game-breaking.

Regarding the ending: there’s a chance you might not unlock the final achievement. I recommend saving manually just before the very end (specifically during the final "mammoth" segment), just in case—the outro screen froze on me, and I had to replay an entire hour of content using an autosave (xd).

Also, regarding that final achievement—"Master Collector" (the PlayStation equivalent is "Earn All Trophies")—there’s a chance it might not pop for you. My current stats show 44 out of 45 achievements unlocked.

Aside from that, I didn't notice any other bugs; I was able to play through the game smoothly.

It’s a short, solid little game that offers a unique twist on the "digging" mechanic. It’s a nice concept, though nothing earth-shattering—much like many other games out there.


I certainly had my fun with it. I won't assign a numerical score as a rating...

...since everyone defines what makes a game "good" differently.

All I’ll say is that I didn't run into any major issues or in-game bugs. Therefore, I can recommend this game to anyone who enjoys this genre and is simply looking to have a nice, relaxing time—why not give it a shot?

Csillámporos kék takony lepte alagutakba mászkáló, mamut-összerakó, szibéria-szimulátor.

[h3]Játékról:[/h3]
A játék egyszerű, kellemes, és lehet mellette relaxálni.
Mindössze annyi a dolgod, hogy olvaszd a havat, találj jégbe fagyott dolgokat, s vidd kiolvasztani majd rakd a helyére.
Ennyi.
Van 3 eszközöd. Az olvasztó puska, ami a sima fehér havat olvassza el.
Tesla puska, ami a kék hó elolvasztására alkalmas.
Illetve egy közönséges ásó, az a pár darab kis földes lyuk kiásására.
Az olvasztó puska meg a tesla fegyó fejleszthető, ezek üzemanyagot fogyasztanak.
Ingyen feltöltheted az üzemanyagot, de a tartalék-készletet meg kell vásárolnod.
Rendelkezésre állnak fény-rúdak, hogy bevilágítsd a sötét helyeket, mélységeket, ezeket megvásárolhatod.
Illetve gránát is, melyekkel eltorlaszolt falat tudsz kirobbantani, és persze a havat is felrobbanthatod.

A hóban szemét van elrejte, sok, amiket eladhatsz, így lesz pénzed, melyből fejlesztheted az eszközöd, a hidegellenállásod, vagy a leltár-kapacitást.
Nagyon sokat kell fordulni, hogy mindig eladj és feltöltsd az üzemanyagot, nagyon sokat.
De hát, időd van, nem hajt a tatár, nincs ellenség a pályán, semmi veszély.

Egy mamut csontvázát kell összerakni, és gyűjteni relikvákat, s persze, bár nem tudom, mire jó, de az olvasztót is fejlesztened kell.

Időnknént pakourozni kell a játékban, illetve kapsz majd egy kampós horgot, amivel lőhetsz a plafonra, és áthintázhatsz, áthúzhatod magad a mélységek felett, vagy akár ki is húzhatod magad belőle.
Bár nem mindig jó, de gyors utazásra is használhatod.

Hatalmas terület áll rendelkezésre, amit hótalanítani kell.
Bár elsőre nem tűnik úgy, és a játék elején nem is lesz így, de amikor bejön a kék hó, jönnek vele a hatalmas üregek, amik dugig van hóba rejtett szeméttel.

A hó inkább valami nyálkára hasonlít, főleg a kék.
Csillámporos kék nyálka. Gyerekeknek lehet venni elvétve ilyen ragacsos nyálkát, mint a gyurma, de még se az, inkább takony. Na, az jut eszembe róla.

Mivel fagyos területen vagy, ezért fontos, hogy csinálj meleget, ahol csak lehet, kis kályhákat begyújtani, hogy ne fagyj meg.
Az ásatási területeknek különböző fagy-szintje van.
1-től 3-ig.
Az egyes fagyszint a leggyengébb, szépen lassan kihűlsz, de van időd mindenre is.
A 3-as fagyszint pedig hatalmas falatokba rágja meg a testetrészeid, míg végül mindent megfagyaszt. Azaz sokkal-sokkal gyorsabban éred el a teljes kihülést, mint az egyes szinten.
Amikor fagyni kezdesz, a karakter lelassul, nem tudsz szaladni, talán ugrani sem, nem emlékszem.
Mint a való életben.
Az, ahol hideg, fehéres fújások vannak, az a terület rendszerint hidegebb, 3-as  szintű.
Mivel a játékban iszonyat sok hiba van, ezért ezek a fagyszintek se úgy működnek, ahogy.
Lehet könnyítés, ki tudja. Például, az egyes megállónál , ha bemész a szélfújta alagútba, ott 3-as fagyás van, de amikor jössz ki onnan, már csak 1. Ki érti ezt.

A játékot át lehet szaladni.
Nem kötelező mindent kifejleszteni, elég lehet csak a fagyellenállást felfejleszteni, az kell, esetleg az üzemanyag kapacitást, és ezzel is simán ki lehet vinni a játékot.
Egyszerűen csak nem ásol ki minden centimétert, nem adsz el mindent, nem nézel meg mindet, csak mész előre, felszeded, amit fel kell, azt jónapot.
Ezzel kb 3 órás lehet a játékidő.
Enélkül 6-8 óra lehet. Midnen azon múlik, mennyire akarod aprólékosan megolvasztani a havat, hányszor kell oda-vissza szaladgálni, mennyi idő, míg másik utat keresel, stb. 
A címke kiírása lelenére a játék nem sandbox.
Legalább is én nem éreztem annak.
Fix terület van, fokozatosan nyílnak meg területek, ahogy megnyitod a kapukat, megkapod a fejlesztéseket, eléred a területeket.
Nem fúrhatsz ott, ahol akarsz, nem azzal, amivel akarsz, stb. Ez nem sandbox.

[h3]Megéri-e?[/h3]
Hát... Megérheti, de!
A játék nem problémamentes.
Sok baj van a mentési-rendszerrel.
Nincs steam-cloud-save.
Grafika itt-ott hibázik.
A játék eszi a CPU-t mint a vaddisznó.
Eltűnik a fegyver vagy a mentés.
És mások.
Van rá sok panasz. Idővel biztosan kijavítják őket, remélem.
Például azt, hogy midnen alkalommal, mikor elindítod a játékot, beböltöd a mentésed, ne kapd meg újra meg újra az "új nyersanyagot szereztél" értesítést, amikor már 5 játékórája szedegeted fel, és ismered.
Elvileg javítoták, hogy a mentési fájl ne resetelődjön. Ne vesszen kárba a játék, de felhőmentés még nincs.
A Mentés iszonyat lassú, mázli, hogy figyelmeztet erre a játék, mert ilyenkor megáll az egész. Nem egy kellemes része a játékélménynek.
És a kegyetlen hardverzabálás... nem is értem a dolgot.
Jó, nem olvadt meg a gépház edzett üvege, de akkor se kellemes.

Magadnak kell eldönteni, megveszed-e vagy sem.
Én azt javaslom, hogy kövesd a frissítéseket, a témákat, és mindig nézd meg, hogy alakul a játék, vannak-e és milyen hibák vannak-e, hogy azokkal együtt tudsz-e élni vagy sem.
No de, egy játék se indul zökkenőmentesen. 

Mindettől függetlenül kellemes, laza kikapcsolódást nyújt a játék.

Very mixed bag but for the price I can recommend it. Early progression is fine but my GOD the labyrinthian way this level sprawls out is far too ambitious for the type of game this is.

Becomes such a chore because progression isn't linear, only gated by  a single upgrade which is really weird given how it plays almost exactly the same just changes the color of what you're "melting" (you're digging. There's nothing to support the idea you're melting ice especially given you're shooting a massive flamethrower but your heat is drawing down while doing so).

Most of the level is covered in trash pickups which flood your inventory forcing you to backtrack a lot, you can't upgrade the fuel storage item capacity so once you hit max upgrades you still only have 2 reloads to use despite money being pointless. It's really difficult to tell when you're in a "high value" area because it's arbitrary, you have to check how much the items you're picking up are worth and decide to "farm" there vs progressing through an area that's worth far less.

Trapped in the new ice age world called Meltopia, you might think it’s a death sentence—but no. This isn’t about survival mechanics; it’s a cozy mining adventure for gamers who want to relax while uncovering archaic items and intriguing valuables hidden in thick ice.

The fun lies in passing through obstacles and discovering hidden locations, though completing collections can feel anticlimactic—except for the mammoth bones, which serve as a strong narrative driver. What keeps me playing is upgrading my arsenal and gleefully saying, “Astalabista, baby ice!” Still, once weapons are maxed out, I wish there were options to spend money on room aesthetics or other meaningful upgrades.

Level design has its quirks: finding a shovel after already carrying two ice-melting guns feels questionable, especially since it could have been available in the store. Despite these oddities, exploring Meltopia remains engaging for its price point.

Meltopia may lack the challenge expected from a miner’s journey, but it intrigues with its scrap-collecting dopamine hits. It’s a cozy, atmospheric game that rewards curiosity more than skill, making it a good pick for players who enjoy relaxed exploration over high-stakes survival.

It's missing a few things. 

Personality, Intrigue and Satisfaction.

I've played both Powerwash Simulator games, and this game just doesn't create any similar feelings. You're plopped into an environment with no context that almost feels Ai generated. There's no story to be found...melting the snow just doesn't feel fun. I fully upgraded the melt gun and honestly it feels the same as the beginning...maybe just slightly faster but no more interesting. 

The music is Meh-core, and mechanics feel unpolished, the progression is uninteresting. 

I hope this game gets a complete overhaul because the concept is interesting and has potential, but right now I have no desire to keep playing.

Hab Meltopia soeben komplett durchgespielt und es hat mir sehr gut gefallen. Wer Spiele wie PowerWash Simulator oder "Digging A Hole" Spiele mag, wird auch dieses mögen. Es ist dieses angenehm entspannte, befriedigende Gameplay: Schnee schmelzen, Ressourcen finden, neue Bereiche entdecken und dabei einfach abschalten.

Die Welt bzw. Atmosphäre wirkt ruhig, geheimnisvoll und motiviert immer wieder dazu, noch ein Stück weiterzugraben bzw. weiter zu schmelzen. Genau diese Mischung aus Entdecken, Sammeln und „nur noch diesen Bereich fertig machen“ funktioniert richtig gut.

Ich habe das Spiel komplett in VR mit UEVR gespielt — und für mich war das großartig, auch die Steuerung ist hervorragend. Gerade das direkte Zielen mit der Heat Gun und das Erkunden der verschneiten Umgebung fühlen sich in VR extrem immersiv an. Für mich fast so, als wäre das Spiel heimlich für VR gemacht worden.

Klare Empfehlung für alle, die solche „satisfying“ Explorations-/Cleaning-/Digging-Spiele mögen. Hoffe es gibt noch mal weitere Levels oder ein DLC.

Je l’ai acheté à 4,67 € au lieu de 7,79 €, et à ce prix-là je le recommande. Même à son prix normal, je trouve que ça reste correct. Par contre, au-dessus de 10 €, j’aurais eu plus de mal à le conseiller.

Le jeu peut faire penser aux jeux de type “dig hole”, mais avec une approche différente : ici, on ne creuse pas simplement à la verticale pour descendre toujours plus bas. On progresse en explorant des chemins, en débloquant de nouveaux passages et en comprenant petit à petit comment avancer.

Ce que j’ai aimé, c’est surtout cette découverte progressive : chercher les chemins, comprendre où aller, se creuser un peu les méninges pour débloquer tel ou tel élément, puis avancer en récupérant de nouveaux items. L’ambiance fonctionne bien aussi : c’est froid, glacial, et on ressent vraiment la pression de l’hypothermie si on ne se dépêche pas.

La difficulté est moyenne, jamais vraiment bloquante, mais assez agréable pour donner envie d’explorer.

Par contre, j’ai eu quelques points négatifs. Au début, le jeu ramait beaucoup, probablement à cause des nombreux items cachés dans la glace. Plus j’avançais, moins le problème était présent, et à la fin je n’avais quasiment plus de latence.

Le endgame m’a aussi un peu déçu. Quand on a beaucoup exploré avant la toute fin, certaines mécaniques perdent un peu de leur intérêt. C’est dommage, car elles auraient pu rester utiles plus longtemps ou être mieux exploitées dans la progression.

J’aurais aussi aimé que le jeu soit un peu plus long, avec peut-être quelques énigmes supplémentaires. La fin apporte une conclusion à l’histoire, mais je n’en dirai pas plus pour ne pas spoiler.

Attention aussi après la cinématique de fin : quand les crédits apparaissent avec les infos sur les personnes qui ont fait le jeu, évitez de cliquer. Chez moi, cela a figé l’écran et j’ai dû relancer le jeu via Steam.

Dernier petit regret : je n’ai pas réussi à obtenir le succès “Master Collector”. Il me manque un item, et malgré plusieurs retours dans les chemins, je n’ai pas réussi à trouver ce que j’avais raté.

Au final, c’est une bonne petite expérience d’exploration, courte mais agréable. Je recommande surtout en promo ou au prix actuel, mais pas si le jeu dépasse les 10 €.

Because of that, you either have to keep running back and forth to sell items instead of melting more snow, or use all your fuel and leave a bunch of loose items lying around everywhere. It also ends up feeling like you spend most of your time saving money just to afford the next storage upgrade.

In the beginning my heart was so cold I kicked an innocent snowman for some firewood. Then, flamethrower in hand I set out to loot what I could from this place. As the snow gave way to my blaze, though, I realized I was slowly melting away the ice inside my soul. I played this game for the satisfaction of completionism yet walked away with so much more. 11/10 for the added bonus of the warm fuzzies I now feel.

A game about Melting some snow

Meltopia is a game in a VERY similar vein to "A Game About Digging a Hole".  That is, a zen-like game with no real fail state that tasks you with clearing out a maliable object mesh using provided tools, while grabbing whatever falls out to sell so you can make faster progress.

While this game is similar, I'd say that it's essentially bigger and better in every way.  The ONLY thing that might turn you off from this game as compared to that one, is that most of your digging will be done horizontally rather than vertically (though you do go up and down on occasion)  Serious, this game is probably 4-5 times larger than A Game About Digging a Hole, and while it is also a bit goofy, it's got a more satisfying ending. (Though, playing either of these games for the story is missing the point).

While I think this game is just about perfect, that doesn't mean it doesn't have issues.  First, it defaults to the Unreal Lumen Lighting engine, which is notorious for running poorly. (Luckily, you can swap to a different system that runs exponentially better and, in my opinion, looks better as well).  Second, this game has a LOT of seem issues.  None of these seems in the geometry caused me any issues, but they are more than a little noticible, and I wish the developers would clean them up a little.  Something as simple as adding an extra mesh every here or there to remove the ability to see between these seems is all that's really needed.  The game has a poorly optimized save system.  Every so often (maybe 10 minutes or so) the game will auto-save, but the auto save will freeze your whole game for several seconds, regardless of what you're doing, to accomplish the save (saving manually is the same, but you choose when to do it)  There was one instance where I was actively melting something when the save popped and when the game resumed, the rest of the snow became invisible.  Finally, and this is more of a minor issues, the game has a fun upgrade system, but once you move onto a certain item, you'll never be required to use the old one ever again.  It just feels a little unsatisfying to fully upgrade an item, and shortly after no longer have use for it.  Adding some extra pockets of snow in certain areas after clearing out the blue snow could make it feel more satisfying, especially when you have just moved to the new item and it takes a long time to make progress.

Outside of those (really fairly minor) issues, this is a great little game to chill out and enjoy.  The only other thing I want is more.  I hit the end of the game, and I was hoping that there would be more (it's not too short of an experience, it's just enjoyable enough that I wish the game had even more content)

If you want a simple game that you can play to relax or get that Powerwasher satisfaction kind of feeling, this game is for you.  I really feel like this should blow up more considering it's essentially just a better version of A Game About Digging a Hole

Un juego relajante y entretenido, no había jugado un juego así, de mejorar tus herramientas al paso que exploras desde hace muchísimo.

Vas mejorando tus herramientas mientras viajas por una mina helada, en ella descubres artefactos de colección, y huesos de mamut entre otros. La finalidad de todo esto es, no solo mejorar tus herramientas al máximo, si no encontrar todos los coleccionables y huesos de un mamut que tienes en la zona principal del juego, a lo cual, una vez encontrados todos, se termina el juego (ahora explico que c*ño paso con esto ultimo)

El juego se basa en descongelar el hielo con las herramientas necesarias, aquí hay 3 herramientas principales. Un lanzallamas; útil en el principio pero luego estupid*mente tercermundista al final (ahora lo explico) Un especie de derretidor de hielo pesado mediante ondas, lo mas util de mediados hasta final de juego; lo ultimo, una pala cochambrosa que solo se usa en una parte y pa nada mas XD.
El lanzallamas por un lado, es lo primero que nos dan, lo usamos para derretir la nieve, el problema con esto, es que el lanzallamas lo usamos muy poco, al cabo de 2-3 horas de juegos, ya solo usamos y necesitamos, el ondas plásmicas, el cual usamos toooodo el resto del juego, sin excepción a volver a usar el antes mencionada, JAMÁS lo volvemos a usar de nuevo. La pala es literalmente, para una parte de la mina y ya...
La forma de mejorar tus herramientas es, mientras derrites la nieve o el hielo, se van descongelando piezas que cuando vamos a los puntos de venta, nos dan dinero para mejorarlas. La verdad que aquí hay otro dilema importante. Si bien es cierto que sobre todo al principio usamos mucho el dinero para mejorar las herramientas, a mediados tirando a finales del juego, nos embolsamos una cantidad est*pida de dinero que no podemos usar para absolutamente nada mas, también podemos mejorar el aguante al frio, el combustible de nuestras herramientas y la cantidad de piezas para vender, de nuestro inventario pero todo esto se hace bien mediados tirando al final del juego por lo que tenemos cantidades absurdas de dinero inútil.
En cuanto al mapa, es muy intuitivo y con lugares bastantes bonitos (es una mina no se puede hacer mucho más) pero si que muchas zonas carecen de algún interés para el jugador mas que pasar de un lado a otro.
La progresión en el juego es rápida, no tardas mucho en completar tus mejoras, y a lo poco que ahorras empiezas a disfrutar más el juego puesto no tienes que ir y venir de un lugar a otro constantemente a vender tus piezas para tener dinero y espacio.

En resumen... un juego que por 5€ le echas una media de 5-6 que es lo que tarde en pasármelo. Lo genial de este juego, es que te pones un video o un podcast de fondo y te lo pasas de tranquis...

Notas mais aprofundadas (contem spoiler):
1) detalhes: 
- O som quando passa na caverna onde há jatos faz um som com atraso.
- Nas opções de idioma está "brasileiro". dá para entender e não incomoda, mas é só um detalhe, normalmente se encontra como "PTBR" ou "Português Brasil"... eu colocaria como "Português mais legal" kkkkkkkkk
2) O que gostei:
- Exploração.
- Colecionar artefatos diversos ("Skull dragon" me fez rir)
- Grande avanço na melhoria das armas, onde dá para ver novos componentes sendo instalados permanentemente.
- Easter eggs, como o da bolota colecionável em referencia a "Era Do Gelo".
3) Sugestões:
- Há elementos que contam uma historia: um esqueleto numa cabana subterrânea. Uma faca presa a documentos. Mas isso não leva a nada... mas poderia. Talvez fazer um mistério macabro? a quem pertenceu esse esqueleto? 
- Mais fazes em busca de esqueletos de outros dinossauros? 
- Achar itens congelados que são peças de quebra cabeça para abrir passagem.
- Uma forma de atingir gelo acima, como uma escada ou forma de controlar a altura da corda do gancho.
- Seria quebrado uma fogueira que iluminasse e permitisse trabalhar por mais tempo longe da fonte de calor principal?
- modo multiplayer, com direito a jogar bola de neve no amigo.
-Mapa ou forma de marcar os tuneis da caverna pra se localizar.
- Depois que se obtém todos os upgrades... não há mais motivação para se ter dinheiro, logo, sem motivação para limpar cada centímetro de neve das cavernas como no inicio do jogo. A principal mecânica do jogo é limpar a neve da caverna, sem isso parece que o jogo perde algo. Entendo que o jogo está novo, mas um endgame mais elaborado nesse sentido seria bom. uma outra necessidade para juntarmos dinheiro... ter uma nevasca que quebre a casa principal e ter que concerta-la talvez? algum pet para alimentar? financiar uma pesquisa que dura algum tempo?
-jogar fogo na dinamite para detona-la no tempo desejado.
4) O que nao entendi:
- O que muda evoluindo forno principal? só ganhamos dinheiro? ele poderia aquecer fontes de calor em outros pontos, nos permitindo sobreviver mais tempo ou abrir passagens importantes. 
- Porque há um robô na casa? e porque não podemos interagir com ele? ele nos trás de volta quando desmaiamos de frio, gostaria de dar um "oi" ou "obrigado", pelo menos.

[h2]Wunderschönes, kurzweiliges Erlebnis![/h2]

Mir hat Meltopia wirklich sehr gut gefallen! Für alle, die sich fragen, worum es im Kern geht: Man erkundet die Umgebung, sammelt fleißig Ressourcen und nutzt diese, um weiter voranzukommen. Das Highlight für mich war dabei das Fortschrittssystem – das Upgraden der Werkzeuge ist absolut optimal und motivierend gelöst. Man kann es ein bisschen vergleichen wie die meisten Buddel Spiele, nur das alles aus Eis ist und es meistens Gerade ausgeht statt Gerade runter. 

[b]Meine Eindrücke:[/b]

 [h3]Grafik & Leistung: [/h3] Optisch ist das Spiel wirklich wunderschön und liebevoll gestaltet. Auch technisch gibt es nichts zu meckern, die Leistung ist top und das Spiel läuft wunderbar flüssig.

 [h3]Audio: [/h3] Die Musik und die Soundeffekte sind richtig gut umgesetzt und tragen toll zur entspannten Atmosphäre bei.

 [h3]Spielzeit: [/h3] Es ist eher ein kürzeres Game, aber genau das macht es zum perfekten Spiel für zwischendurch. Man wird nicht mit endlosen Aufgaben überhäuft, sondern bekommt ein kompaktes, rundes Erlebnis. Man hat immer ein Motivierenden Spiel fortschriet. 

 [h3]Fazit: [/h3] Wer ein optisch ansprechendes Spiel mit tollem Upgrade-Loop für ein paar entspannte Stunden sucht, ist hier genau richtig. Klare Empfehlung von meiner Seite !!

Natürlich ist der Weg einem vorgegeben, also es gibt bislang nur lange Gänge. Ob da noch was größeres gibt, weiß ich derzeit nicht.

Die Waffen brauchen Sprit und wir unsere Wärme. Das heißt, unterwegs fängt man an zu frieren und muss auf seine Anzeige links aufpassen. Ansonsten erfriert man, was quasi der Tod ist.

Ansonsten gleiches Spiel, wie bei anderen Buddelspielen. Man findet Zeug und verkauft es, füllt seine Sachen auf und Stuft seine Ausrüstung hoch. Artefakte gibt es auch, die aber glaube eher nur wegen den Erfolgen da sind. Ich habe es für unter 4€ gekauft und da kann man absolut nicht meckern.

[h1]Melting My Way Through a Chill Adventure[/h1]

Meltopia takes that same kind of simple satisfaction you see in similar games like powerwashing or digging holes and makes it its own. Melting through snow and ice, slowly uncovering paths and seeing where they lead, ended up being more satisfying than I expected. I never felt rushed. I just took my time exploring, checking corners, and making sure I didn’t miss any routes or hidden spots. By the end, it felt really rewarding knowing I had found everything.

What I liked most is the atmosphere and the small details. As you melt the snow, you sometimes uncover things like blood stains or skeletons, maybe from previous explorers, which adds a bit of mystery without making it stressful. Finding artifacts along the way kept things interesting, and the ending cutscene was short but a nice payoff.

It’s a very chill experience overall. You can explore as much or as little as you want, and it never feels pushy. There were moments where I forgot about my warmth and had to panic-run back to a stove, but even that felt more funny than frustrating.

I know there were some issues at launch with bugs and missing achievements, but the developers have been active with communication and patches. As long as the gameplay worked, I was already having a great time. I spent hours on day one just melting through caves, even without achievements working. Overall, it’s simple, enjoyable, and you can really feel the care put into it. Good work.

So many resources can be scavenged from the snow/ice, this is more of a transportation simulator than anything. There's also the tesla gun, with how much it was used I feel the game should have been called teslatopia. I thought the meltgun would be upgraded or you'd find a better meltgun. The digging  mechanic is absolutely horrendous, the constant clicking for minimal progress. Yeah I can use dynamite but it's not the same. I was never really concerned about freezing and only did so after finishing the game for the achievement. I didn't know what to expect story wise so the ending was a surprise, though it makes me wonder about the lore of the world. Overall, I'm happy with my purchase and don't regret buying the game. не рекомендую игру. сначала ты играешь такой: прикольно, прикольно. а  потом ты получаешь новое орудие для бурения снега и начинаешь его заново качать а из за малой прокачки оно работает по малой области, и ты стоишь как идиот и копаешь зарабатывая по несколько долларов, потому что оно жрёт всю твою энергию за секунды. ну представим ты дотерпел прокачал это хавно, после прокачки оказывается что уже докачиваешь всё что есть. и теперь ты не убираешь весь снег который видишь а на пофиг буришься через снег что бы найти лёд с предметами. Satysfakcjonująca, piękna i niesamowicie relaksująca!

​Meltopia to absolutna perełka dla fanów spokojnej eksploracji. Gra wciągnęła mnie bez reszty, a mechanika roztapiania śniegu i lodu w poszukiwaniu fragmentów mamuta oraz ukrytych artefaktów daje niesamowitą frajdę.

​Co najbardziej mi się podobało:

​Grafika: 
Oprawa wizualna stoi na bardzo wysokim poziomie. Kontrast mroźnej bieli z detalami odkrywanymi pod lodem robi ogromne wrażenie.

​Płynność i sterowanie: 
Technicznie gra jest dopracowana perfekcyjnie. Wszystko działa płynnie, a sterowanie jest intuicyjne i precyzyjne, co tylko potęguje przyjemność z rozgrywki.

​System postępu: 
Oprócz szukania kości mamuta, zbieranie surowców na ulepszenia sprzętu i odkrywanie tajemniczych artefaktów sprawia, że zawsze jest coś ciekawego do zrobienia.

​To idealny tytuł, żeby się wyłączyć i pograć we własnym tempie. Jeśli szukasz gry, która łączy świetną jakość wykonania z "odmrażaniem" sekretów starożytnego świata – zdecydowanie polecam!

​Moja ocena: 10/10

If you're at all interested in this game I think you'll expect a certain level of jank to it, so that's not really my issue with this. The issue is that the gameplay is just dull and doesn't really give you the drip feed of dopamine as similar games. Instead of digging in different directions to actively go after treasure, you're basically just digging in a straight line until you hit a wall, and then you dig in a different direction. It doesn't feel like you can optimize your digging/explore further than the linear path. In terms of progression the loot values don't really change and it looks like you can max out the upgrades pretty early on.

I also liked the progression — upgrading your tool makes you want to push further and unlock new areas. Exploration feels engaging and rewarding.

Another great thing is how meditative the game feels — you can just relax and enjoy the process. 
Overall, the game leaves a very positive impression. It’s a great idea, well executed. I’ll definitely replay it every winter.

Did you like 'A Game About Digging A Hole'? Learn to Fly? Powerwash Simulator? This'll scratch that itch the same way getting McDonalds will scratch an itch for meat. Not bad, but don't expect the world.

If you're leaning towards post-dad-games like Powerwash, don't bother trying to 'clean' everything spotless. You'll have your best time with this game upgrading as you go and hunting for things to melt in the furnace. These are key items that are mostly found by keeping an ear out for the audio queue of 'Angelic Chanting'. Which can be drowned of by the wind sometimes, but not often. 

There's some half-hearted attempts at parkour sections that all feel pretty abnoxious when you see them exclusivley after unlocking the grapple hook. Just feels like bigger rooms to trek across. There's actually a few sequence breaks where you can just hook up to the end of a "Grapple the cieling three times" challenge and grab the thing in one. You are not here for parkour.

I also spent most of the time listening to comedy specials with the game sound turned down, but not off. It's a decent 'occupy your hands' game. Probably could have done a weeks worth of online course lectures while playing.

Without spoiling the ending, it is delirious. Makes me think of those bad phone game ads, you'll know what I mean when you see it, should only take you an afternoon if you aren't picking through every little pile of ice. You aren't here for the story, I'm not here for the story. It's fine. But, god did it still surprise me.

I'd say to get it on sale, but honestly even at full price, it's a higher budget flash game for playing while you listen to a podcast or a few albums you've been neglecting. If you're willing to pay this much for a movie ticket, then you should be fine getting stoned and putting some old cartoons on to melt some ice and grapple-hook around for a few hours.

Meltopia не кричит. Она шепчет. Она не гонит тебя вперёд счётчиком кислорода или голодом — просто расстилает перед тобой бескрайнее белое одеяло и вручает в руки тепловую пушку. И тут ты понимаешь: снег — это не враг. Это дверь. Миллион дверей, которые ждут, когда их откроют.

Добро пожаловать в мир, где холод — лишь декорация, а главное сокровище спрятано глубоко внутри ледяного сердца планеты.

С учётом того, что игра только вышла, она уже довольно неплохая. Это расслабляющая игра, которая никуда не гонит и ничего от тебя не требует. Жанр здесь можно назвать «симулятор археолога-выживальщика». Ты выходишь на локацию с одной целью — плавить глубже, находить ресурсы и артефакты, улучшать снаряжение, чтобы процесс шёл быстрее.

Я получила колоссальное умиротворение, играя в Meltopia. Мне очень понравилось. Иногда в такие игры просто необходимо играть, чтобы расслабиться и отключить голову))

Пишу данный отзыв после 100% прохождения (ачивку за все ачивки на момент отзыва не дают 4.05.26)
Для кого данная игра спросишь ты?  
Любишь зиму? Отлично, эта игра с зимней атмосферой для тебя.
Не любишь зиму? Отлично эта игра тоже для. Растопи весь этот мерзкий снег, что встанет у тебе на пути и приблизить поскорее приход лета.
Ставь "душевно" если любишь зиму и "огонь" если любишь лето, посмотрим кого больше.

А если отставить шутеечек, то что игра из себя представляет?
Ты простой парень, набредаешь  на особняк, в котором твоя главная задачи собрать все кости мамонта.
И тут уже вступает в силу основной геймплей изничтожение снега всеми доступными способами с последующей продажей всякого найденного хлама скупщику.
А для уничтожения снега и для нашего выживая в этих холодных местах у нас есть снаряжение:
- Мелтган, наше основное оружие добрую половину игры, дышит огнём и прокачивается на базе, в последствии мы меняем её на тоже самое, только в другом скине, прогрессию то в игре надо держать. использует топливо при использовании.
- Тесла, второе оружие, тот же мелтган, но для другого снега, прокачивается на базе. Использует топливо при использовании. Есть у этой пушки забавная особенность, которую я заметил, если держать зажатой кнопку стрельбы, то периодически можно слышать разные звуки пуков, не знаю зачем вам эта информация, но меня позабавил саундизайн пушки. 
- Последнее завершающие основное оружие и самое сильное, думаете это какая то крутая супермегапушка и вы абсолютно правы, она требуется для очень редких и твёрдых мест и имя этой великой имбе "ЛОПАТА", да просто лопата, прокачка отсутствует, топливо не использует.

Так же у нас существую вспомогательные вещи:
- фонарики, дают освещение там где она требуется, стоит копейки, пропадает через некоторое время.
- динамит, устал медленно убирать снег основным оружием? Тогда этот малыш тебе поможет, делает бум по радиусу и сразу собирает шмотки тебе в инвентарь в радиусе взрыва.
- крюк кошка, позволяет цепляться на возвышенности и быстрее перемещаться по локациям.
- канистра с топливом, твой бро на долгих вылазках, позволяет полностью восстановить топливо в основном оружии.  

Если ты являешься игроком, который копит и нехотя тратит валюту, то можешь со спокойной душой покупать динамиты, канистры, свет. При полной зачистки игры у меня осталось 250 тыс. валюты, а динамиты я раскидывал только в путь и так же в какой то момент оставлял лут для продажи лежать на земле, потому что не хотелось бегать туда сюда ради продажи, валюты и так в большом достатке и тратить её особо некуда. 

Также в игре присутствует активная способность по уничтожению снега на добротном расстоянии и абсолютно бесплатная, она секретная, нашёл её сам и с вами поделюсь. Ставите в настройках автосохранение на минимальное кд в 1 минуту, потом в моменте когда игра включает отсчёт до автосохранения, ты подходишь к снегу и зажимаешь основную пушку и водишь легонько мышкой по области в момент фриза, когда фриз пройдёт, ты увидишь предметы в воздухе и зону без снега, просто постреляй в предметы и они заберутся. На начале игры это сильно экономит время.

А так это довольно медитативная игра на пару вечеров (я потратил около 10 часов, но я вычищал весь снег на локациях) за небольшой прайс, если хотите поиграть во что простенькое и расслабиться под приятную музыку, то она для вас. А если хотите игру поострее, то выключите музыку в игре и включите какаю-нибудь страшную, ощущения сразу будут другими.

Meltopia by Garden of Dreams is a calm, exploration-focused experience that builds its identity around a single, deceptively simple idea and expands it into something quietly engaging. Set in a vast frozen landscape, the game invites players to interact with the environment in a way that feels both tactile and transformative. Instead of pushing constant objectives or high-pressure challenges, it leans into a slower rhythm, encouraging players to explore, experiment, and uncover what lies hidden beneath layers of snow and ice.

The central mechanic revolves around melting and clearing the environment, turning what initially appears to be a static world into something dynamic and responsive. Players gradually carve paths through thick snow, revealing underground spaces, resources, and fragments of a larger mystery. This process becomes the backbone of the experience, offering a steady sense of progression as more of the world is uncovered. Tools evolve over time, allowing for faster or more creative ways to interact with the terrain, which helps maintain engagement as the player delves deeper into the landscape.

Exploration is handled with a strong sense of freedom, giving players the ability to move at their own pace without rigid constraints. The world is filled with hidden areas, subtle environmental clues, and scattered points of interest that reward curiosity. Rather than relying on explicit guidance, the game trusts players to follow their instincts, gradually piecing together both the geography and the underlying narrative. A loose overarching objective provides direction, but it never overshadows the act of exploration itself, which remains the primary focus from beginning to end.

One of the more effective aspects of Meltopia is how it uses environmental contrast to keep the experience engaging. The open, snow-covered surface areas convey a sense of isolation and stillness, while the spaces beneath introduce a different atmosphere, often more enclosed and visually varied. This layered design gives the world a sense of depth, both physically and thematically, reinforcing the idea that there is always more to discover beyond what is immediately visible. The transition between these spaces feels natural, adding to the immersion without relying on dramatic shifts.

The pacing is intentionally relaxed, which will resonate strongly with some players while leaving others wanting more intensity. There are no strict time limits or constant threats pushing the player forward, allowing for a more meditative experience. This design choice creates a sense of calm that is rare in many modern games, but it also means that engagement depends heavily on the player’s willingness to embrace a slower, self-directed style of play. Those looking for fast progression or frequent action may find the experience too subdued.

Visually, the game adopts a clean and stylized approach that prioritizes clarity over complexity. The snowy environments are simple but effective, using color and lighting to create a consistent atmosphere. As players move into underground areas, the visuals gain more variety through changes in texture and lighting, helping to break up the monotony of the surface. The overall presentation supports the gameplay well, ensuring that important elements remain easy to identify while maintaining a cohesive aesthetic.

Sound design plays a subtle but important role in shaping the experience. Ambient audio, such as the sound of wind across the snow or the quiet dripping of water in hidden spaces, reinforces the sense of isolation and discovery. Music is used sparingly, allowing the environment itself to take center stage. This restrained approach enhances immersion, making each moment feel more grounded and reflective.

Despite its strengths, Meltopia does face some challenges in maintaining long-term engagement. The core mechanic, while satisfying, can begin to feel repetitive over extended sessions, especially if players do not encounter new variations or discoveries at a steady pace. The lack of structured objectives can also lead to moments of uncertainty, where players may feel unsure of their next step. These elements are part of the game’s design philosophy, but they may limit its appeal to a more specific audience.

Overall, Meltopia succeeds as a focused and atmospheric exploration experience that prioritizes discovery and player-driven progression over traditional gameplay structures. It offers a unique take on environmental interaction, supported by a cohesive visual style and a calm, immersive atmosphere. While it may not cater to those seeking constant action or clearly defined goals, it provides a rewarding experience for players who enjoy taking their time and uncovering a world piece by piece.

review:
Despite sharing some mechanics with your Keep Digging/A Game About Digging a Hole, etc., and indeed adding a couple of interesting mechanics, like a grappling hook, this game just doesn't have the sauce. The assets are all the same marketplace objects you've seen in a hundred other games (Tavern Simulator, Ale & Tale Tavern in particular). The movement is stilted - momentum and acceleration feels wrong. This is particularly noticeable once you get the grappling hook. It just feels dissatisfying.

The grind isn't too terrible, but you will completely max out all upgrades about halfway through the game, and you definitely feel yourself wanting to be able to become more powerful. Part of the fun of digging games is late/postgame upgrades that make you godlike.

Plenty of menu jank. For example, if you change any options on any submenu, it unchecks the "invert y axis" option. Not an issue for most, as few people use inverted y, but it's an indicator of what you're getting into here. Achievements don't award correctly (I have 45/46 achievements. The last one? "Get all other achievements").

I can't confirm, but I suspect AI textures, music, and/or writing is involved. Has a slop kinda feel to it.

All that said, if you're super into digging games, this isn't a bad way to kill 5-6 hours with a 2nd screen activity going. Wait for a sale.

I randomly tried the demo and already found the concept very interesting.
The full game confirms it: the developers have listened to the players, and I think the game still has huge potential for growth.
However, it lacks crafting, housing, and more progression options to enrich the long-term experience. The world feels a bit empty, almost like a frozen desert (no pun intended).
The sound design is quite good overall, although the music sometimes lacks a bit of flavor and grandeur.
The absence of enemies contributes to the charm of the game and reinforces its relaxing atmosphere, but adding other types of danger beyond environmental hazards could bring more tension.
The game mainly revolves around searching for and discovering artifacts: it’s interesting, but it eventually feels like something is missing. More context about these artifacts — what they are, what they represent, what they used to be, and who created them — would add real depth to the experience.
In the same vein, exploration would benefit from more lore: finding notes left by dead or missing survivors, or traces of the past, would make the world feel much more alive.
And finally, when will there be a French localization?
Despite all that, the game remains very chill and easy to get into.

I played for just under 2 hours, hoping the gameplay loop would feel a little better as I got more upgrades for the systems in play, but that feeling never came unfortunately.

You spend your money upgrading your capacity for your flamethrower so you can get through areas faster, don't need to backtrack as much for tank refills, upgrading your inventory capacity so you can hold more before you need to run back through the maze of tunnels you're not creating, but unearthing because it's all set in indestructable stone instead of a large freeroaming area where you can make your own setting and uncover secrets.

Once you get an actually satisfying amount of upgrades for your flamethrower, whoops; too bad here is flamethrower 2.0 that feels like sh*t to use now because you're back to square one, the same kind of terrain to move through only all the upgrades you've invested in are useless; do it all again but it costs more, and you're stil just finding ample amounts of junk worth $1-10 each with a 41 slot inventory, and your next upgrade is $8,000, but you need to make sure you're upgrading your:
- Ability to even be outside
- Inventory Capacity
- Ammo Capacity for EACH gun, they don't share upgrades
- Gun rank so it doesn't feel like you're using a wet noodle
- Consumables like flares for tracking your movements, Dynamite which is only useful for set points to open up a shortcut or progression direction

ALL of these systems cost more and more the more you touch them (except consumables), and your loot barely increases in worth at all. You end up having to do 6 laps back home for ONE of those upgrades to the next stage, and that feels like crap.
The rare stuff you're supposed to feel good about finding in the wild? Here is a useless piece of a trophy, here is $100 gold from a chest to add to your $6k you made finding it, here is a helmet you'll stick onto a plinth and like it. No upgrades for your guns, no consumables to use, no temporary powerups to feel good while you adventure, just trash; the whole way through. Nothing felt good to do, nothing felt good to upgrade.

The English translations are grammatically incorrect pretty much everywhere, and just having a single Native English Speaker do a pass over all of the games text would notice that and have it fixed quickly.

I imagine the further I get into the game, and the more quick travel points I unlock, I would get a third flamethrower reskin, and have to start again with the upgrades because that's what they want for progression. Upgrading your Forge? Does nothing but a little boost in cash.
Finding an Artifact? Cosmetic. Stick in on the plinth it belongs on and never look at it again. No permanent buffs, no cash, no upgrades to my gear.
No map, minimap, markers of any kind. Your ability to navigate is as simple as how you remember the tunnels you've dug, and where you chose to throw some WHITISH-BLUE FLARES ON WHITISH BLUE SNOW OR BLUEISH WHITE ELECTRIC SNOW.

It really just isn't fun, like at all...

I just simply cannot recommend this game to play in good faith, it's just boring beyond belief in the time I gave it right before I could refund it. I tried GoD, I tried to enjoy your game, but you really made it difficult to find any actual fun in the game.

Edit: Because the devs actually seem to be quite invested in the reviews and are reading and replying all the negative ones. Here is what I would want to see in the game to make it a bit more fun and have some staying power:
- Perks and Perk Slots. Let me use your "Artifact Chime" to follow the direction into little baubles I can attach to my guns (much like the gun upgrade system where each upgrade straps a unique piece or replaces a piece to your gun, that actually was a cool feature I liked). Let me have a wider but more shallow flame, let me fire a burst of flame at the cost of fuel, let me have a flame that ricochets off indestructable walls and into destructable ones, let me have a hotter flame that burns blue and deeper but narrower to find walls and secrets through strip mining, let me be able to swap these perks in and out of weapons using unlockable slots so I have something to look forward to.
- Skill Tree. Let me unlock experience for my guns/player as I clear snow. Give me sprint dashes, double+ jumps, price increases on my loot, perk slots, snow boring consumables and snow grenades, spelunking eyes within range to see rare items/money items through walls for increasing ranges. The player power is simply [Upgrade Gun Generic Upgrade, Grapple Hook] that I found in 2 hours of play. That sucks beans and doesn't respect the players time, doesn't reward exploration because every pathway is set in stone.
- Danger! Danger in this game is simply [Didn't go home before bar went down, go home] and [Grapple through slightly colder corridor for 3 seconds, but don't worry it's not slightly colder on the way out]. You have no health, no risk of death from falling or cave ins, no frozen enemies to uncover; it's just boring.
- Uses for the Forge Upgrades, and Artifacts. Why do I bother running all these things back to base when they do absolutely nothing? Why have I found a hardhat deep in the snow, that sits on a pedestal and...just exists? Why doesn't upgrading the huge forge give a burst of heat outwards and melts 100% any of the lower grade snow around the main base so I don't pick apart all the little pockets of nothing? 
- The Story/Theme. Like...what even is this place? You had me come in through the front door of an open field after I Mobile Game knocked down a snowman and took WOOD from it to start, then that same front door is immedaitely blocked off with...Not even the same world? Like what the hell is even happening. Your story is non existent and nonsensical. Uncovering a minecart track I can't actually walk down, or random Generic Dungeon Room 1 with 150 gold in it, is not building a world.
- Temporary Power Ups. 30 seconds where I fire fireballs that blow up chunks of the world, movespeed bonuses, moving through snow while I'm on fire for 10 seconds, ANYTHING fun to break up the gameplay loop of "Bag Full, go back and get $600 gold for the next $2600 Upgrade for either of the 4 upgrades you want that is a marginal increase; go back and do it again"
- Story beats and Story Telling through frozen scenery. Perfectly intact dungeon room 1 is not story telling. There are notes on the walls of cabins that can't be read. Crates that are fireproof with no loot. Nothing is destructable besides Snow and Electric Snow (in the first two hours). Chest rewards suck, I don't want 20 seconds of flame thrower currency as a chest reward when i only stumble upon a chest every 15 minutes.
- Sound Design. Getting the generic snow currency that is planted in every 3 feet of snow isn't a satisfying sound and doesn't feel good to gain, nor does really anything in the game. Even hearing the "Artifact Chime" and heading towards it as it gets louder, only to find a piece of BIG TROPHY or $150 gold really puts a damper on the player, especially given we've got to walk the thing all the way home without having our weapon available to us.
- Bug Fixing. If my flamethrower was active during a Save Game screen OR a tutorial window (those are actually fantastically made whoever made them, good work!) means my gun is burning through fuel during time where I don't have control of my character. My bag upgrades display 41/5 when I logoff and log back on.

I'm glad the devs are listening, reading, and doig their best to make their game fun and bug-free, but this is not a completed game by any stretch of the imagination. I hope you guys can add some fun systems and big open spaces to the game for us to tunnel through like bugs, because the crafted tunnel world plugged with snow right now is just not it sorry guys.
Thank you for reading this wall of text, if you made it this far, kudos to you for being REALLY interested in this game and thoroughly vetting reviews properly

Locations are very tight and are insanely similar, which makes it easy to just turn around and lose sense of direction.

Из пожеланий на доработку:
- возможность устанавливать фонари, а не только кидать (особенно нужно для ям)
- местами длинноватые шахты без возможности скинуть лут и рюкзак на 100 не спасает
- добавьте больше уровней прокачки хотя бы рюкзака
- механику замерзания не поняла - просто медленно ползешь. Было бы прикольно иметь какую-то штуку с экстренным, но временным прогревом (типа стопки перцовки). Один раз замерзла на совсем, когда тащила ледяной куб, в остальное время можно было замерзать бесконечо.
- непонятно зачем мы улучшаем основную печь (есть подозрение, чтобы открывать новые улучшения) - добавьте какое-то оповещение "теперь ваш доступно то-то" (пройдя игру стало понятно, но можно и промежуточные успехи игроку выдавать)
- для заправки хотелось бы иметь возможность делать это в один клик как с загрузкой лута в ящик. Сейчас это три клика - открыть меню, ткнуть в заправить и кнопку выхода из менюшки. В моменты когда время копания меньше минуты (с непрокаченным оборудованием) эти 3 клика надоедают
- по локациям везде намазана кровь, есть какие-то записки, но к чему это не понятно, хотелось бы иметь чуть больше лора. Зачем и как мы сюда попали кроме как собрать мамонта. Чья это кров и что там в записках)
- шахт много и если память не блещет, то легко забыть где уже был, где есть неисследованные места. Может какие-то карты или заметки помогли бы. Или хотя бы возможность ставить указатели.
- после того как в руки берем не пушку (например кусок льда или кидательное снаряжение), то после взаимодействия в руках оказывается огнемет, а не то что было в руках до того (хотя справа на быстрых клавишах отображается выбранным то устройство, что было в руке до того). Учитывая, что большую часть времени мы используем теслу, то постоянный возврат к огнемету неудобен
- еще вспомнила, что холодные комнаты работают забавно - на входе определяется 2-3 снежинки, а вы выходе обычно одна :) да и в целом часто снежинки в одном и том же месте по разному отображаются
- еще поймала сейчас, что показывает цену улучшения теслы, а кнопка не тыкается и непоянтно почему. Ощущение, что должна появится новая пуха для которой это улучшение, потому что такое же поведение было на огнемете до того как теслу нашла (игру прошла, поведение так и не изменилось)
- автосохранение из-за которого игра подвисает на несколько секунд довольно спорное решение. возможно его сделать незаметным?
- механика копания ям тут несколько убивает процесс. Нужно постоянно кликать мышку, улучшений для лопат нет, постоянно пар застилает видимое пространство, там вечно темно (фонарик часто сложно кинуть чтоб помогал). Когда плавка снега в тех же объемах занимает несколько секунд, а тут нужно несколько минут непрерывного кликанья - это уже не про удовольствие от игры, к сожалению. (Выкопав все ямы вспомнила про динамит :()

Второй мой обзор на эту игру. Первый был негативным, так как хотелось поиграть сразу с релиза и урвать первые ачивки, но баги не дали насладиться. В итоге, достижения подвезли спустя день-другой, когда они были уже у всех. Но, не смотря на то, что в дорелизном трейлере нам показывали несколько иное - нерастопленный замок, вмерзшего в лёд робота, открывающего нам двери на вершине лестницы, после того, как мы его растопим (в релизной версии он просто продаёт нам предметы) - игра, по итогу прохождения, оказалась весьма неплохой. Своим медитативным геймплеем она действительно расслабляет. Музыка погружает в некий транс, и вот ты уже не заметил, как несколько часов к ряду аутируешь растапливая пиксельный лёд. Немного хромает баланс, ибо за 15 часов методичного вычищения всех локаций под ноль (на соточку), полная прокачка всего, чего только можно была уже на шестом. Металлолом копился без надобности, а рюкзак раздражал своей маленькостью. Серьёзно, 100 слотов - это мало, при том, что оставленные на земле вещи пропадали по возвращению к ним.
В целом игра хорошая. Не без грехов, но видно, что старались. Спасибо, было интересно.

This game has a lot of faults but it's clearly made with passion and effort was absolutely put into the game.

The positive is that the game is simple and straightforward and it feels like it rewards you for your time - progress does not feel like it's a chore and it comes quickly. The game also is about exploration and curiosity and what you discover feels like it's worth the effort to get there. When you unlock a new area, it actually feels like a massive relief and a reward for the work it took to get there.

The downsides are quite numerous, though. There are a ton of bugs that range from annoying to game breaking. It seems the devs are aware of disappearing weapons (which would end your game), but I'm still seeing many more. 

[list]
[*] The shovel doesn't dig dirt at all - I ended up just using dynamite which negated the whole need for the shovel.
[*] If you're holding down the "primary attack" and then switch to dynamite, it will use your fuel up while you're throwing the dynamite.
[*] If the dynamite animation gets interrupted because you're moving and change elevation, it won't throw the dynamite and will stick until you swap weapons.
[*] After throwing dynamite, it always switches your weapon back to the Flamethrower which is *insanely* annoying when you need to use the Tesla gun. However, the Flamethrower ends up working on the snow that only the Tesla gun can hit, so I'm wondering if this is just a graphical glitch.
[*] If you "freeze" and need to be rescued, it takes a long time for your unlocks to be put back to where they should be and you keep moving slower as if you're frozen.
[*] MASSIVE ONE! [b]THERE IS NO AUTO SAVE![/b] You [b]MUST[/b] manually save before closing the game or, if your computer is prone to crashing, you need to manually save often, otherwise you'll become very upset very quickly.
[/list]

There's also a lot of "nit picks" such as grammatical errors on load screen tips. You also are upgrading the furnace but are never told why you are. I'm not at the endgame so I imagine that might be a final step. The main area is beautiful but not utilized in any way. Also, if there is one I haven't found it, but this game is in dire need of a map. There are forking passages and multiple paths that you're not always meant to go down the second you reach them, but you need to find hidden artifacts and it's impossible to remember where and how much you've cleared out. It also doesn't help that the only indicators of the artifacts are audio, so if you're listening to music, Youtube, podcast, Audiobook, etc. then you're gonna be struggling to clear every literal square inch to find everything.

I could go on but for the price, this game is absolutely worth putting up with. It's clearly a passion project and not just a cheap asset flip with no purpose that has flooded the genre lately. I'd highly recommend the game and I hope the developers keep working on this. It's almost there as one of the best that the genre has to offer, but it needs a huge coat of polish before I can call it that.

developer_response: Thank you so much for such a detailed and fair review. We’re really glad you enjoyed the melting, upgrades, artifacts, and overall value. review:
If you like melting snow away with a flamethrower, this game is for you. It is oddly satisfying and actually a lot of fun. Its a mix of simulation + slight narrative + collecting artifacts + upgrades without a tedious grind. It took me 8 hours to finish, and thats with max upgrades and all artifacts found, all for $5 so it makes it completely worth it imo. 

Things they can improve on:

- The dynamite blast radius could be bigger. For example, when clearing a large cave, it makes it difficult to break the items stuck at the ceiling. In a smaller cave, you can just jump with your gun to grab them but in a large cave, it becomes unreachable. You could make it so the dynamite sticks where you throw it, that way we are able to get items that are at ceiling level. 

- This could also be applied to the glowstick. My biggest gripe is that it never stays where you place it so it would be a huge upgrade to have it stay where you put it. 

- Which leads to my next point: the game is too dark for my liking. But I don't believe there was a setting to increase brightness. Would be great if this was added. 

- Inventory cap at 100 is not enough mid to late game. Especially in areas where the run back to the closest sell box is quite far away. Would be nice if you increased it to 150. 

- The shovel issues have been reported and likely being worked on. But what's nice is that you can use dynamite in place of it.

- Would be nice if the items/artifacts we found had descriptions. Or the letters in the rooms we found had actual written notes. I think it would make the game so much more interesting and immersive. 

Overall, its a great game. Just needs QoL upgrades to make it even better.

review: Relaxing vibe

A little bit janky, not very long (depending on how pedantic you are in clearing everything) and fairly shallow in respect of story and mechanics.

But it's not meant to be super deep or long, and other than achievements not working properly, I had no issues. Looks good, plays well, and is a nice, chill, relaxing game where you can just plod along at your own pace. And of course, the price is right.

Would recommend if this sort of game suits you.

Good fun for four bucks! Took me 8 hours to basically 100% the game, did all of the objectives and cleared all of the snow. I can recommend at the sale price. For 7 bucks though, i dunno. It's got some issues. I'll start with the positives.

[h3]Positives:[/h3]
[list]
    [*]Looks nice (if a bit dark sometimes)
    [*]Runs well (my computer is pretty nice, so your mileage may vary)
    [*]Addictive incremental game loop
    [*]Upgrades that feel substantial
    [*]Learning the map is really fun, unlocking shortcuts happen right when you're starting to think you need one and it feels cool zooming through tunnels knowing exactly where you're going and the best way to get there.
    [*]Map areas that are distinct and recognizable
    [*]The overall feeling that at any point in your dig it could open into an interesting doorway, shortcut, or mysterious area (which it often does)
    [*]The length is good. I didn't feel short changed, nor did it overstay its welcome.
[/list]

[h3]Negatives:[/h3]
[list]
    [*]FIXED The achievements didn't work for me. They said they fixed it in a patch that I installed after completing it, I didn't get the achievements on loading my save though and I'm not gonna 100% it again. Kinda sadge.
    [*]No FoV option
    [*]There are clipping issues with lots of rocks that looks unprofessional, none that I was able to clip through though. Getting stuck in the geometry was not an issue.
    [*]KINDA FIXED There's one jumping puzzle that's infuriating. By default, sprint is a toggle so don't hit shift to run, you'll just toggle run on and off. Then when you jump and bump some geometry it bounces you like crazy, couple that with one jump at the top of a parkour bit that you're almost guaranteed to bump your head on and fall all the way down, it's really frustrating.
    [*]I can't be sure, but it seems like if you keep digging while your inventory is full, the resources don't all stay on the ground, causing you to lose out on money that is finite on the map. There is plenty on the map, but the fear of missing out caused me to feel like I needed to sometimes do a long runback even though I had 2/3 fuel left.
    [*][spoiler]What's up with the artifacts? I was expecting something to happen when completing the sets but nothing did til the end when I finished the mammoth. Are they required along with the mammoth? Are they just for the achieves I didn't get?[/spoiler]
    [*][spoiler]Same deal with the boiler upgrades, just getting money was a little unsatisfying after the first couple[/spoiler]
    [*]FIXED [spoiler]The shovel sucks. I used dynamite for the dirt mostly, but I got all the snow dug and really wanted to dig all of the dirt, but I wasn't going to jump in place to do it. Really would've loved an upgrade or two for the shovel even if they were 50k+, I ended the game with 200k leftover[/spoiler]
[/list]

I played the demo, and the developers have made a lot of changes since then. Mostly for the better. It's especially surprising how quickly they did it.
Many new mechanics have been added that weren't there before.
Even though the game is relatively small, there's plenty to do.
The game is based on the core mechanic of melting snow, and you'll be doing a lot of that.
The visual style is fantastic!
It's not without its flaws, of course. The game has room to grow.
However, given how responsive the developers are, I think both the game and the team have a bright future.
If you enjoy something unhurried, calm, and straightforward, and you also adore adventure, you can definitely pick it up. Especially at this price. 
A pleasant evening or two are guaranteed.
